text: Last winter I photographed my mum's tablet strip so I'd remember what the doctor gave her. Now I can't recall the name. I searched 'tablets' and 'medicine' and got nothing at all. I finally found it by scrolling through December — it's a sharp, clear photo of the strip, so search just doesn't see it as medicine.

evidence.primary_stage: search just doesn't see it as medicine

expected.why: Cue ('medicine') was CORRECT and the photo is a clear picture of one; nothing came back even though it was there → the index never recorded the concept. 5.2.

text: Last winter I photographed my mum's tablet strip so I'd remember what the doctor gave her. Now I can't recall the name. I searched 'medicine December 2022' and got nothing at all. I finally found it by scrolling — it was actually from January 2023. One month off and search threw it out completely.

evidence.primary_stage: One month off and search threw it out completely

expected.why: The subject cue was correct; the MONTH was wrong, and the wrong cue eliminated a correct target → hard filter. The user's wrong date does not make it Stage 2 (spine boundary note: wrong cues are part of 'vague').

text: Last winter I photographed my mum's tablet strip so I'd remember what the doctor gave her. Now I can't recall the name. I searched 'medicine' and got hundreds of results — pharmacy bills and screenshots first. The strip was in there, about 300 photos down, and I only found it after scrolling for ages.

evidence.primary_stage: The strip was in there, about 300 photos down

expected.why: The target WAS returned, just buried under clutter → ranking. 5.4.

text: I remember a photo of a tiny café in Goa from a trip, no idea which year. Searching 'goa' shows the beach photos but never the café. When I finally found it by date, the info panel had no location at all — my GPS must have been off that day.

evidence.primary_stage: the info panel had no location at all

expected.why: The place cue was right, but the photo carried no location, so no query on place could reach it → index. 5.2.

text: I remember a photo of a tiny café in Goa from a trip, I was sure it was 2019. Searching 'cafe goa 2019' showed nothing. When I dropped the year and searched 'cafe goa' it was the first result — the trip was in 2018.

evidence.primary_stage: When I dropped the year and searched 'cafe goa' it was the first result

expected.why: Removing the one wrong cue brought it straight back → the wrong year acted as a hard filter. 5.3.

text: I remember a photo of a tiny café in Goa from a trip, no idea which year. Searching 'goa' gave me something like two thousand photos, mostly beach. The café photo was right at the bottom of the results; took twenty minutes of scrolling to get to it.

evidence.primary_stage: The café photo was right at the bottom of the results

expected.why: Returned but ranked at the bottom → 5.4.

text: I need the fridge receipt for the warranty; I think I photographed it in 2021. I searched 'receipt 2021' — nothing. The receipt itself says March 2021, but my brother had sent it on WhatsApp and Google Photos had it dated June 2022, the day the folder finally backed up.

evidence.primary_stage: Google Photos had it dated June 2022

expected.why: The user's date was RIGHT; the stored date was wrong → index. Contrast tri-C-53, where the user's date is wrong. 5.2.

text: I need the fridge receipt for the warranty; I think I photographed it in 2021. I searched 'fridge warranty receipt 2021' — nothing. Just 'receipt' found it immediately. Every word I added seemed to make search stricter, not smarter.

evidence.primary_stage: Every word I added seemed to make search stricter, not smarter

expected.why: Adding cues made the target vanish; one cue alone found it → AND logic shrinks recall. 5.3.

text: I need the fridge receipt for the warranty; I think I photographed it in 2021. Searching 'receipt' gives me every bill I've ever snapped and they all look the same as thumbnails. The fridge one was there, but somewhere past the first hundred.

evidence.primary_stage: The fridge one was there, but somewhere past the first hundred

expected.why: It was retrieved, then crowded out by look-alikes → ranking. 5.4 (6.4 also true, but ranking came first).

text: I need the plumber's visiting card I photographed at some point. I don't remember when he came, which month, or even what the card looked like. I just don't know enough about it to search for anything.

evidence.primary_stage: I just don't know enough about it to search for anything

expected.why: No words would help: there is nothing remembered to put into them → Stage 2.

text: Looking for a birthday photo with a chocolate cake. Whose birthday, which year, whose house — none of it is there any more, it's been too long. It could be any of fifty birthdays.

evidence.primary_stage: none of it is there any more, it's been too long

expected.why: The cues decayed and blur with similar events → memory, not expression. Stage 2.

text: There's a plant at my aunt's place I photographed on one of our visits. I can't remember which visit, and apart from 'big leaves' I can't picture it well enough to describe it.

evidence.primary_stage: I can't picture it well enough to describe it

expected.why: They cannot picture it: the memory itself is missing → Stage 2, even though they also can't describe it.

text: I remember the photo exactly — my son asleep at the dining table with noodles stuck to his cheek. I can see it perfectly. But what do you even type for that? I tried 'sleeping boy' and gave up.

evidence.primary_stage: But what do you even type for that?

expected.why: The memory is vivid and complete; the block is turning it into words → Stage 4.

text: I know exactly what the flower looked like — bright orange, trumpet-shaped, on a vine by the gate. I just don't know what it's called, so I had no idea what to type. Ended up scrolling through the whole of 2022.

evidence.primary_stage: I just don't know what it's called, so I had no idea what to type

expected.why: They KNOW the thing and lack only its name → 4.3 no_word_for_thing, not 2.4 word_for_the_thing (that value_boundary is exactly what this tests).

text: Needed the photo of my prescription. I remembered it clearly — the white box with the blue stripe. Searched 'prescription', then 'medicine', nothing. Took ages scrolling, finally found it by searching 'tablet'.

evidence.primary_stage: finally found it by searching 'tablet'

expected.why: Memory was fine; the right word was the system's word, not theirs — a vocabulary barrier ([CTX] §7.2's own example). Stage 4.

text: I remember a pic of a small café in Goa from a trip, no idea which year, search for 'cafe goa' shows nothing.

evidence.primary_stage: search for 'cafe goa' shows nothing

expected.why: [CTX] §7.2 row 1 and arch §3.2's worked example: core, Stage 5.

text: Needed the photo of my prescription, took ages scrolling, finally found by searching 'tablet'.

evidence.primary_stage: finally found by searching 'tablet'

expected.why: [CTX] §7.2 row 2: core — utility, vocabulary barrier, eventual success.

text: Searching my wife's name shows nothing even though face grouping is on.

evidence.primary_stage: Searching my wife's name shows nothing

expected.why: [CTX] §7.2 row 3: a PRECISE cue that failed → adjacent, not core.

text: My WhatsApp photos never got backed up so I couldn't find the one from my brother's wedding.

evidence.primary_stage: My WhatsApp photos never got backed up

expected.why: [CTX] §7.2 row 4: explained entirely by library state → adjacent (Stage 0).

text: Searching 'dog' shows my dog's photos fine, but I can't find the one where she's wearing the yellow raincoat, from a couple of monsoons ago. Scrolled through two years and quit.

evidence.primary_stage: I can't find the one where she's wearing the yellow raincoat

expected.why: Harder: search 'works' at the category level, but the known item is reached only through a partial perceptual cue and a fuzzy time → core.

text: Search for my sister's name only brings up about half of her photos. The other half are there if I scroll, she's just not recognised in them.

evidence.primary_stage: she's just not recognised in them

expected.why: Harder: a person search failing looks like a retrieval story, but there is no known item and no vague cue — general search quality → adjacent.

text: I took a photo of the parking level sign yesterday at the mall. Search 'parking' shows nothing, so I just opened yesterday in the timeline and it was the third photo.

evidence.primary_stage: Search 'parking' shows nothing

expected.why: Harder: utility and a search failure, but the user knew EXACTLY when — precise retrieval → adjacent.

text: Asked Ask Photos for 'the houseboat photo from our Kerala trip'. It confidently told me it was from 2019 and showed a completely different boat. I'm honestly not sure of the year myself, maybe 2017 or 2018.

evidence.primary_stage: It confidently told me it was from 2019 and showed a completely different boat

expected.why: Harder: the user's own year is a range (vague) and the system answered with false confidence → core, Stage 5.

text: Spent an hour searching 'grandpa birthday' and scrolling 2019 for the photo of grandpa cutting his cake. Nothing. Then I realised my old phone's camera folder was never backed up — it's not in Google Photos at all.

evidence.primary_stage: it's not in Google Photos at all

expected.why: The search failed too, but it FIRST went wrong at Stage 0: nothing could have found it. The dramatic hour is not the first failure.

text: Looking for our Coorg trip photos from 2020, I was certain of the year. 'coorg 2020' returned nothing. A friend said the trip was 2021 — I'd mixed it up with another trip. 'coorg' alone had them all.

evidence.primary_stage: 'coorg' alone had them all

expected.why: Memory was wrong AND the system hard-filtered. One correct usable cue ('coorg') was present, so per the spine boundary note this is 5.3, not Stage 2.

text: Searched 'wedding' for my cousin's mehendi photo. Got hundreds, the right one was way down, and even when I got there the thumbnails were so small I scrolled past it twice.

evidence.primary_stage: Got hundreds, the right one was way down

expected.why: Ranking (5.4) failed before recognition (6.4) → Stage 5 comes first.

text: I didn't even bother with search, it never works for me. Scrolled through years of photos looking for the one of our old house before it was sold. After an hour I gave up.

evidence.primary_stage: I didn't even bother with search, it never works for me

expected.why: Gave up (Stage 8) but FIRST chose not to search (Stage 3). The invisible-failure population.

text: The photo from the evening we got the news about my dad's job. I know exactly the moment but there's nothing in the picture that says 'news'. I typed 'family evening' and got everything and nothing.

evidence.primary_stage: there's nothing in the picture that says 'news'

expected.why: The query was poor because the cue is not visual → Stage 4 precedes the Stage 5 response.

text: Searching 'beach' found the right trip straight away, but not the exact sunset photo. I kept retyping 'beach sunset', 'sunset sea', 'evening beach' and never thought to open one and swipe through. Gave up.

evidence.primary_stage: never thought to open one and swipe through

expected.why: Search and recognition worked (the trip was found); the failure was recovery — no anchor-and-pivot → Stage 7.

text: At the bank counter they wanted my PAN card and I knew I'd photographed it, but searching 'PAN' and 'card' showed nothing. The queue was waiting behind me.

evidence.photo_class: At the bank counter they wanted my PAN card

expected.why: Taken to keep information, needed to extract it → utility.

text: Looking for the whiteboard photo from last quarter's planning meeting — the one with the roadmap. No idea which week, and 'whiteboard' shows 200 near-identical boards.

evidence.photo_class: the whiteboard photo from last quarter's planning meeting

expected.why: Whiteboard notes → utility.

text: My grandfather passed last month and I want the photo of him laughing at my graduation. Search his face brings up old ones but not that one, and I don't remember which year I graduated from which course.

evidence.photo_class: want the photo of him laughing at my graduation

expected.why: A moment and a person → sentimental.

text: I photographed my nani's handwritten recipe card for her dal years ago. I want to cook it and also to keep her handwriting. Can't remember when I took it and 'recipe' finds nothing.

evidence.photo_class: I want to cook it and also to keep her handwriting

expected.why: Both purposes are STATED → both. Would be 'utility' if only the recipe mattered.

text: Can't find the video of my daughter's first steps, somewhere in 2020. Searching 'walking' or 'baby' only shows photos.

evidence.media_type: Can't find the video of my daughter's first steps

expected.why: Video-only → adjacent, reason video_out_of_scope ([CTX] §15.1, P3-INV-9).

text: From my sister's wedding there are photos and a few videos. I'm after one PHOTO, the family group on the stage steps, but search keeps surfacing the videos first.

evidence.media_type: there are photos and a few videos

expected.why: Involves both, target is a photo → mixed, stays core (EC-CODE-17).

text: I screenshotted a delivery address someone sent on Instagram a few months ago. 'address' and 'screenshot' in search find nothing useful.

expected.why: Screenshots are IN scope ([CTX] §4.1) → core, screenshot.

text: Goa trip wali cafe ki photo dhoondh rahi hu. Cafe ka naam yaad nahi, year bhi pata nahi. 'goa cafe' search kiya toh kuch nahi aaya.

evidence.primary_stage: 'goa cafe' search kiya toh kuch nahi aaya

expected.why: Same shape as the Goa example, in Hinglish; span must be the Hinglish text.

text: Mummy ki dawai ki photo li thi pichle saal, ab doctor naam puch rahe hai. Search me 'dawai' likha, kuch nahi mila. Aakhir 2 ghante scroll karke mili.

evidence.primary_stage: Search me 'dawai' likha, kuch nahi mila

expected.why: The India hypothesis 2 ([CTX] §15.3): a Hindi query failing at parsing → 5.1.

text: Bhai ne shaadi ki photos WhatsApp pe bheji thi, woh Google Photos me hai hi nahi. WhatsApp folder ka backup hi nahi hua tha.

evidence.primary_stage: WhatsApp folder ka backup hi nahi hua tha

expected.why: Hinglish twin of [CTX] §7.2 row 4 → adjacent (Stage 0).

text: Bas itna yaad hai ki baarish ho rahi thi aur hum chai pee rahe the. Kaunsa saal tha, kaun kaun tha, kuch yaad nahi. Kya search karu samajh hi nahi aa raha.

evidence.primary_stage: Kaunsa saal tha, kaun kaun tha, kuch yaad nahi

expected.why: Not enough remembered to form any search → Stage 2. The last sentence reads like Stage 4 but the cause stated is memory.
